newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia welcomes new UN secretary-general.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia welcomes new UN secretary-general.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Monday his country welcomed the election of Kofi Annan of Ghana as the next United Nations secretary-general.
"Indonesia welcomes the choice of Kofe Annan. He has wide experience in the United Nations. He is very qualified," Alatas told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
"Indonesia hopes Kofi Annan, who came from Africa...will show sensitivity to the problems faced by the developing countries and Non-Aligned Movement," he said.
Ghana and Indonesia were founding members of the 113-nation Non-Aligned Movement, which Indonesia chaired until October 1995.
Alatas said he would check with the new secretary-general whether regular dialogues sponsored by his two predecessors between Indonesia and Portugal over the East Timor issue would be continued.
"This is something that we will check. It is expected that the new secretary-general will continue those things implemented by his predecessor, but we will see," Alatas said.
Alatas said he will visit the United Nations on December 21 where he was scheduled to meet with his Portuguese counterpart Jaime Gama to discuss East Timor.
"I do not have high expectations about this meeting as it is to review what has been achieved during the last eight meetings," Alatas said.

East Timor, with a population of more than 800,000 people, was invaded by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed by Jakarta a year later in an act not recognised by the U.N., which still regards Lisbon as the territory's administering power.
